name: Iron-rhodium
equilibrium_context: G-type antiferromagnet below roughly 350 to 370 K, ferromagnetic above; first-order metamagnetic transition with wide hysteresis
summary: Calibration point of the registry: a thermal shortcut to a phase that is stable anyway. Anyone reporting a new case should be able to show that it is not an FeRh.

driven_states.emergent_property: A femtosecond pulse generates ferromagnetic order: nucleation within about one picosecond, formation of macroscopic domains and of the accompanying lattice expansion on 10 to 100 picoseconds. Within the hysteresis the ferromagnetic phase persists after the pulse.
driven_states.source: Ju, Hohlfeld, Bergman et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 93, 197403 (2004), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.197403
driven_states.caveat: Borderline case, deliberately included. The ferromagnetic phase exists in equilibrium above 370 K; the light merely triggers the transition ultrafast instead of creating an inaccessible state. Whether a non-thermal, ultrafast contribution exists has been debated for more than twenty years and is not settled. Hence mechanism thermal and equivalent_equilibrium_state yes.

threshold.quantity: fluence threshold; the starting temperature must lie close enough to the transition

further_sources: Mariager et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 108, 087201 (2012), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.087201
driven_states.quenchable_by: heat diffusion, recovery within nanoseconds to microseconds

sources: Ju et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 93, 197403 (2004), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.197403
gaps: Fluence threshold scatters between groups and film thicknesses.
